THE BRIEF

We repair the everyday building defects that interrupt an otherwise busy property. A single damaged door and a list across several tenancies need different preparation. We identify each location, check the surrounding construction and agree the repair and finish before organising attendance.

✺

THE WORK

Start with the defect, then check what sits around it

  • A door rubs or will not latch

    We check the leaf, hinges, frame, latch and closer together. Loose hardware and a damaged fixing need a different repair from a distorted door or frame.

  • A wall or ceiling is damaged

    We establish the affected area, board or surface condition and what must be removed. A water-stained ceiling also needs its moisture source addressed before the final finish is reinstated.

  • Joinery or fittings are loose

    We inspect the fixing points, supporting material and matching parts. The scope distinguishes adjusting or securing an item from replacing damaged components.

THE WORK

One repair, a grouped visit or a larger refresh

Work typeTypical briefWhat we confirm
Single itemA closer, damaged panel or local patch.Size, parts and access.

THE WORK

Match the repair to the existing building

We check hinge and lock patterns, board type, finish colour and sheen. Matching an aged surface, ordering uncommon hardware or opening up concealed backing can change the quote. We confirm these items before allowing for patching, joint treatment and finishing.

  • Boards, timber and substrate

    We confirm the existing build-up and sound fixing areas before choosing replacement material. Repair dimensions and adjacent damage determine how far the work extends.

  • Colour, sheen and hardware

    We use available product details and site samples to discuss matching. The quote identifies where a local finish is suitable and where a larger visible surface needs attention.

THE WORK

From protection to a working finish

  1. 01

    Mark and protect

    We confirm the agreed item list and protect adjacent floors, furniture and finishes before opening or removing affected material.

  2. 02

    Repair and reinstate

    We address the fixing or substrate, install the agreed parts, and complete the specified patching and finishing stages.

  3. 03

    Check and clear

    We check door operation or the repaired surface, clear the agreed work area and record any remaining item requiring separate approval.

THE WORK

Work around the people using the space

We agree keys, room access, noise and dust-producing tasks with your representative. Shared corridors need a usable route, while a painted or repaired surface may need time before furniture returns. These arrangements belong in the work plan, alongside any return visit.

THE WORK

What shapes the quotation

  • Quantity and condition

    The number of locations, repair area, height, substrate condition and matching materials define the labour and material allowance.

  • Access and finish stages

    We itemise agreed protection, access equipment, waste and return visits, so a small repair is not confused with a complete room refurbishment.

THE WORK

A clear record against your list

We identify completed items by room, location or defect number. The handover records the agreed finish and operation checks, available completion photos and any parts or separate works still outstanding.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Does a sticking door always need replacing?+

No. We first check alignment, hinges, fixings, latch and closer. Adjustment or hardware repair may address the issue; damaged door construction or frame conditions can require a different scope.

Can several small jobs be quoted together?+

Yes. A numbered list with locations and photos helps us confirm quantities and materials. We group practical tasks and identify anything needing separate access, parts or a later finish stage.

Can you repair the ceiling after a leak?+

We can include agreed ceiling repairs and finishing. We separate the moisture-source work from reinstatement and check the affected material before confirming the repair boundary.
